newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler Q3 profit per vehicle rises.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler Q3 profit per vehicle rises.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said its third quarter after-tax worldwide profit per vehicle doubled to $982, while average retail incentives in the United States fell to $685 from $870 a year ago.
The U.S. Number Three automaker earned $492 per vehicle in the 1995 third quarter as lower minivan production volume, minivan launch costs and Ram pickup truck production expansion hurt results.

Chrysler reported third quarter fully diluted earnings of $0.93 a share, including a $0.07 charge for early retirement costs, beating the consensus estimate of $0.69. Net earnings were $680 million, after the $55 million charge.
A year ago, Chrysler reported net profits of $354 million, or $0.45 a share, after a two-for-one stock split.
The automaker said its combined U.S. and Canadian retail units sales of cars and trucks, including fleet sales, were 645,766 units in the third quarter, up from 560,841 a year ago.

International retail sales for the third period were 57,209, up 19 percent from 48,207 in the year-ago quarter. Chrysler sold 28,079 vehicles in the third quarter in Europe, a 28 percent increase from 21,918 last year.
